why: Clause 1 (q critical for L_p|M ⟺ q − p ⊥ T_qM) is the same on both sides and transfers both ways: A states it for every slice M (k = 0 included) as (q, p − q) ∈ N, B for dim ≥ 1 with tanN; B ⇒ A handles k = 0 separately. Clause 2 differs in scope and transfers in neither direction: A gives the Hessian of L_p in the project's own parametrization xParam, 2(g − ℓ_{p−q}), at EVERY point (no critical-point hypothesis); B gives the first and second partials of L_p∘x for an ARBITRARY C² map x on an open set, the second ones only where the first vanish, and the form 2(g − t v·ℓ) for p = x + tv with v normal (ℓ = normal projection of ∂²x). Each side's clause 2 is elementary calculus and is proved outright (A_to_B: B2_holds from the project's hessian_normSq_sub_comp, fderiv_normSq_sub_apply; B_to_A: A's Hessian formula re-proved from hessian_normSq_sub_comp, as in the project), so the 'equivalence' uses the hypothesis only for clause 1.
